newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends at day's lows, seeks direction.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends at day's lows, seeks direction.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended at or near the day's lows in an extremely quiet session after a failure to hold on to Monday's impressive gains.
Traders said some bargain-hunting emerged after the benchmark December contract slipped below the previous stiff 980 stg-a-tonne support.

The contract finished at 980 stg, still a 15 stg loss, after dipping to the day's low of 978. On Monday, the December cocoa vaulted to test the psychological 1,000 stg-barrier on active short-covering.
This was reflected in the hefty 1,280 lot-fall in the uncovered December position to 25,082 lots the close of business on Monday.
"The December contract needs fresh impetus to push prices through 1,000 stg," broker GNI said in its daily commentary.
Traders said the market remained starved of fresh news to move prices out of the narrow 980-1,000 stg band.
"It needs fresh news to give an impetus one way or another," the trader said.

Traders said earlier news the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) was seeking bids to buy 4,250 tonnes of its stockpiled cocoa had some dampening effect on the thinly-traded market. The sales were later completed.
Overall volume on the exchange was a small 2,198 lots.
